text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lithuania's Ba2 rating from Moody's for its foreign debt was higher than expected, said Finance Minister Algimantas Krizinauskas. The rating puts Lithuania on a par with emerging markets such as Venezuela, Mexico and the Philippines.
- Lithuania's inflation rate was zero for the first time in its post-Soviet history in August. For the first eight months of 1996 the inflation rate was 10.3 percent.
- The share price of Vilniaus Bank increased by 4.7 percent to 1100 litas as demand continued to exceed supply.
- The World Bank decided yesterday to issue a $19 million credit to reconstruct Lithuania's highways.
- Lithuanian light industry exports are expected to exceed two billion litas this year.

- Vilnius municipality decided to name a small square after the late Chechen rebel leader Dzhokar Dudajev to commemorate the fifth anniversary of Chechen "independence". A Chechnya square will be named in the second city, Kaunas, Friday.
- Bank of Lithuania initiated bankruptcy procedures against Vakaru bank.
- Lithuanian Finance Minister Algimantas Krizinauskas left for Washington on Thursday to negotiate with the World Bank for an $80 million credit.
- Lukoil Baltija opened two more filling stations in Vilnius and Kaunas in September.
- An international exhibition Baltic Textile and Leather opens in Vilnius September 10 and expects 212 participants from 27 countries.
